title: RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome》：研究问题的原文依据。

【The multi-omics series: rationale and objectives · s0001-s2004-p1】The ARPE-19 RNA-seq dataset analysed here (GEO: GSE328981) spans four treatment conditions (CTRL, QMR/RESONO, SECRETOME, QMR+SECRETOME) across 8 H, 24 H and 72 H, in matched oxidatively stressed and stress-free conditions, and has been the subject of five parallel multi-omics analyses. Published and submitted work from this series has established that: (i) QMR restores a fraction of stress-deregulated microRNAs, engaging NF-kB/NLRP3-regulating (miR-590-3p) and anti-inflammatory (miR-146a-5p) programs, while PBD secretome preferentially induces regenerative miRNA signatures [37]; (ii) bulk RNA-seq revealed QMR-driven transcriptional reprogramming of antioxidant defenses (GCLC, GCLM, GSR, HMOX1), mitochondrial fitness and proteostasis [38]; (iii) the lncRNA/circRNA landscape identified QMR as the dominant driver of transcriptomic variance, with circASPH upregulated by QMR and circCRIM1 hyperactivated by the combination [39]; (iv) oxidative stress induces a chimeric-transcript burden that QMR and secretome attenuate at discrete nodes (CTDNEP1, COL7A1, HSD17B7) [40]; and (v) expressed-variant analysis identified QMR as a mitochondrial-surveillance activator (PINK1 induction, DNM1 suppression) while the secretome drove SERPINF1/PEDF upregulation [41]. None of these has addressed the chemical state of the expressed transcriptome. The present study adds two further layers: a HARMLNC-derived map of RNA base modifications and a genome-wide A-to-I editing screen. They are treated as distinct layers because they differ in chemistry, are detected by different tools and are installed by different enzyme families. The aims are: (i) to define the base-modification set detectable in oxidatively stressed ARPE-19 cells and identify positions present across all conditions; (ii) to test whether QMR or secretome alter that set; (iii) to describe its temporal distribution across 8 H-72 H; (iv) to characterize the A-to-I editing landscape and test, with effect sizes and formal equivalence bounds, whether the interventions alter it; and (v) to relate both layers to the five parallel analyses of the same experiment.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Cell culture, oxidative stress induction and experimental design · s0002-s2001-p1】Human ARPE-19 cells (ATCC CRL-2302, Manassas, VA, USA) were maintained in DMEM/F-12 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum, 2 mM L-glutamine and 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin at 37 C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere. Cell-line identity was validated by short-tandem-repeat profiling (PowerPlex 10, Promega; STR concordance > 80%), and cultures were confirmed mycoplasma-free every 2 months (MycoAlert PLUS, Lonza). The design comprised four treatment conditions, no-intervention control (CTRL), QMR electrotherapy (RESONO), patient blood-derived secretome (SECRETOME) and their combination (QMR+SECRETOME), across three time points (8 H, 24 H, 72 H), each sampled in two oxidative-stress conditions. In the stressed condition, sub-confluent monolayers were exposed to tert-butyl hydroperoxide (tBHP; Sigma-Aldrich) at a final concentration of 75 uM maintained continuously; the stress-free condition was handled identically without tBHP. Biological replication was n = 1 per stress condition at 8 H and n = 3 at 24 H and 72 H. Full details of seeding density, treatment scheduling, QMR parameters and secretome preparation have been described previously [37,38]. The base-modification analysis reported here draws on 56 sequencing libraries that yielded at least one high-confidence call, comprising 14 libraries per treatment arm (7 oxidatively stressed and 7 stress-free) and, per arm, 2 libraries at 8 H, 6 at 24 H and 6 at 72 H. The A-to-I editing screen was run on 57 libraries; the single additional library has no counterpart in the modification layer and is retained only in the editing analysis, so editing-layer and modification-layer denominators differ by one throughout. A per-library manifest is provided as Supplementary Table S1.

【Oxidative-stress baseline: the stress-free contrast internal to the cohort · s0002-s2013-p1】Because the corrected library metadata (Section 2.4) establishes that each treatment arm was sampled both under continuous tBHP and in the stress-free condition, the cohort contains an internal unstressed baseline. We used it to ask whether oxidative stress itself alters the positions reported here. For every high-confidence site and for every position of the canonical recoding panel (Section 2.15), non-reference frequency was extracted from all libraries with read coverage at that coordinate, irrespective of whether the position had been called in that library, so that the contrast is a comparison of frequencies rather than of detection events. Stress-free and tBHP-exposed libraries were compared by Mann-Whitney U test across the full set and, in parallel, by Wilcoxon signed-rank test on replicate-matched pairs (same arm, time point and replicate), with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all positions tested. Results are reported in Section 3.10, with per-position depth and testability in Supplementary Table S6 and test results in Supplementary Table S7. An independent stress-free/tBHP library set external to this cohort, used only as a consistency check, is reported in Supplementary Table S8.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · s0005-p1】This study characterizes the chemical state of the RPE transcriptome, comprising both internal base modifications and A-to-I editing, in ARPE-19 cells under oxidative stress and under two non-pharmacological interventions, QMR electrotherapy and patient blood-derived secretome. The base-modification map comprises 241 high-confidence calls across 56 libraries, resolving to 15 unique positions. Its composition is narrow: every class recovered is canonical to transfer or ribosomal RNA, and the contexts are mitochondrial rRNA, rDNA-bearing contigs and the chromosome 21 rDNA cluster. Three positions are constitutive by the definition used here: a modification at chrM:2617 of the mitochondrial 16S rRNA (MT-RNR2), most probably m1A, detected in 51 of 56 libraries at the highest depth in the dataset; an i6A/t6A position at chr6:158,766,314 in an EZR/SYTL3 overlap region carrying the highest non-reference frequency of any site; and a dihydrouridine position on the rDNA-bearing contig KI270733.1. None varies with treatment. Of the 15 positions, 7 support a statistical test and none shows a treatment effect on non-reference frequency (minimum p = 0.19); arm-level differences in this dataset are differences in detection counts, not in modification level. The A-to-I editing layer likewise shows no detectable treatment effect: no window of 940 survives multiple-testing correction, and formal equivalence testing bounds any effect on substitution composition within 1.4% for all arms, and on mean editing frequency within 10% for secretome and combination and within 20% for QMR. A stress-free baseline internal to the cohort, made available by a library-metadata correction described here, shows that with the single exception of MT-ND5 these positions are present at comparable frequency with and without oxidative stress. Re-analysis with three dedicated editing callers reproduces the quantification, recovers a de novo editome with the Alu enrichment expected of ADAR products and confirms at single-nucleotide resolution that no curated position differs between treatment arms; the same analysis identifies the sequencing batch, rather than any biological variable, as the dominant axis of differential editing in this cohort, which we report as a limitation of the design. What the study contributes is a first, bounded description of the RPE modification and editing layers under oxidative stress, together with the finding that neither layer is measurably altered by QMR or secretome at the resolution and sample size available, and an explicit statement of the margins within which that holds. Placed beside the layers at which these interventions do act, that bounded non-interference is itself informative: it is more consistent with action through defined routes than with generalized perturbation of RNA metabolism, and it quantifies, rather than merely asserts, how little of the RNA-recoding layer is disturbed.

sections.text:
《RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Global overview of the RPE base-modification set. (A) Distribution of the 241 high-confidence calls across the six modification classes represented among the 15 unique sites (17 site-class combinations; two sites carry two class assignments). (B) Gene and locus annotation of the unique sites by Ensembl GRCh38 overlap; where two annotations overlap the position, both are shown. (C) Arm-level modification-call burden (CTRL 52, QMR 56, SECRETOME 71, QMR+SECRETOME 62). (D) Binary site-detection matrix, 15 sites × 56 libraries; columns are individual libraries ordered by treatment arm, time point and oxidative-stress condition, rows are the 15 unique sites with their gene assignment; the colour bars below indicate treatment arm and stress condition.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. The three chromosome 6 positions, shown at their true genomic coordinates. (A) Genomic map placing chr6:158,766,313 (m3C) and chr6:158,766,314 (i6A/t6A), 1 bp apart in the EZR/SYTL3 overlap region at 6q25.3, and chr6:31,270,453 (m2G/m22G) in HLA-C at 6p21.33, 127.5 Mb away. (B) non-reference frequency by treatment arm at each position (high-frequency i6A/t6A across all arms; high-frequency m3C where detected; uniformly low-frequency m2G/m22G at HLA-C). (C) detection frequency across treatment arm and time point, with per-cell denominators taken from the library manifest (supplementary Table S1). No panel of this figure asserts a treatment effect; the corresponding tests are reported in Section 3.3 and Table 1.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Detection-count architecture across treatment arms. (A) Shared and arm-restricted site counts: six of the 15 sites are detected in all four arms; single sites are private to individual arms or intersections. (B) Non-reference-frequency profile of chr7:102568040 across arms, with per-arm denominators of 14 libraries (detection counts CTRL 2, QMR 3, SECRETOME 8, QMR+SECRETOME 5). (C) Treatment-associated positions listed by coordinate (chromosome 21 cluster; chr7:102568040; GL000220.1:114669, the single combination-only call, detected at 72 H). (D) The three molecular layers previously described for this dataset (regulatory, structural, chemical), shown as the interpretive frame for the present layer.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Software versions and computational environment · s0002-s2011-p1】Analyses were performed on a high-performance computing cluster (CentOS 7.9) with the following principal software packages: Trimmomatic v0.39, STAR v2.7.10a, Picard v2.27.5, BEDTools v2.30.0, SAMtools v1.15.1; R v4.3.1 with pheatmap v1.0.12, ggplot2 v3.4.2, rstatix v0.7.2, karyoploteR v1.20.0, circlize v0.4.15 and ComplexHeatmap v2.12.1; and Python v3.9.7 with pandas v1.5.3 and scipy v1.10.1 for data integration and cross-caller concordance. The HARMLNC pipeline was executed using the published HAMR framework code with custom adaptations for lncRNA inclusion; Tsniffer Canonical was run with the human reference modification panel (MODOMICS 2022 + RMBase v2.0). Custom scripts are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

【Three orthogonal callers reproduce the editing quantification and detect no treatment effect · s0003-s2011-p1】The editing layer was re-analysed with three dedicated callers (Section 2.16). Three results follow, bearing respectively on the reliability of the quantification, on the treatment question and on what limits this cohort. First, the quantification is reproducible. Across the curated positions REDItools3 and JACUSA2 agree with each other and with an independent pileup of the same alignments to Pearson r = 0.975 to 0.992 at coverage of at least 20 reads, and the two callers agree on the per-library Alu editing index to r = 0.95 (Supplementary Table S14). The de novo scan recovers the expected biology: of 12,376 candidate editing positions, 88.3% fall within Alu elements, an 8.4-fold enrichment over the genomic Alu fraction, whereas germline homozygous positions called from the same libraries show 5.3% Alu occupancy and the curated recoding panel 3.6%, as expected for non-repeat coding positions (Supplementary Table S17). The scan also recovers known recoding targets directly, including NEIL1 K242R, BLCAP Y2C and Q5R, and COPA I164V. Second, and directly addressing the possibility that individual sites might be dysregulated even where bulk activity is not, no site shows a treatment effect. Of the curated positions, 15 reached testable coverage in all four arms; none differed between arms after correction (minimum p = 0.169, minimum q = 0.169; Supplementary Table S15), and the Alu editing index likewise did not differ between arms under either caller (p = 0.82 and p = 0.97; p = 0.97 within the batch-balanced subset). The site-level result therefore agrees with the window-level result of Section 3.7 and with the equivalence bounds reported there. Third, the oxidative-stress contrast reproduces the one positive finding of Section 3.10 independently: at chrM:13710 (MT-ND5) the REDItools3 quantification confirms a lower frequency under stress (q = 0.00055), as does the HLA-C position (q = 0.0035), the latter carrying the allelic caveat of Section 3.3. NEIL1 K242R reaches q = 0.048 on 18 libraries, consistent with the marginal status assigned to it in Section 3.9.
